title: Local fibre bounds on open charts and synchronization along closed comparisons
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set and $(f_i:X_i\to S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. Let $A$ be a finite set. For every $i\in I$ and $a\in A$, choose open subschemes $W_{i,a}\subseteq X_i$ and $V_{i,a}\subseteq S_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion], such that $(W_{i,a})_{a\in A}$ covers $X_i$ and $f_i(W_{i,a})\subseteq V_{i,a}$. Assume transitions $X_j\to X_i$ and $S_j\to S_i$ carry $W_{j,a}$ into $W_{i,a}$ and $V_{j,a}$ into $V_{i,a}$ whenever $i\le j$. Write $g_{i,a}:W_{i,a}\to V_{i,a}$ for the restricted morphism. Fix an integer $d\ge0$. Fibres are scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with dimension $-\infty$ for the empty scheme.

(1) For each $i$, all fibres of $f_i$ have dimension at most $d$ if and only if, for every $a\in A$, all fibres of $g_{i,a}$ have dimension at most $d$.

(2) Suppose additionally that every $g_{i,a}$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and that for $i\le j$ the induced map $W_{j,a}\to W_{i,a}\times_{V_{i,a}}V_{j,a}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then a bound on all fibres of $g_{i,a}$ persists to all fibres of $g_{j,a}$ for every $j\ge i$. Consequently, if for each $a\in A$ there is an $i_a\in I$ such that all fibres of $g_{i_a,a}$ have dimension at most $d$, there exists $j\in I$ such that for every $k\ge j$ every fibre of $f_k$ has dimension at most $d$. Both assertions allow empty fibres, empty schemes, and $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 02FY, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change (1), combined with topology.tex Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions: auxiliary finite-chart propagation and globalization lemma.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $s\in S_i$. For $s\in V_{i,a}$, the fibre $(g_{i,a})_s$ has underlying space $W_{i,a}\cap f_i^{-1}(s)$ with the subspace topology: the open-subscheme identification and the fibre-to-set-theoretic-fibre homeomorphism give this directly. The residue field at $s$ is unchanged on the open $V_{i,a}$ because its stalk is unchanged. For $s\notin V_{i,a}$, $W_{i,a}\cap f_i^{-1}(s)$ is empty by $f_i(W_{i,a})\subseteq V_{i,a}$. Thus these intersections form an open cover of $X_{i,s}$, with the nonempty members precisely among the chart fibres. These identifications preserve dimension: a homeomorphism and its inverse carry strict chains of irreducible closed subsets to strict chains.

source.place: Tag 0055, definition-Krull; open restrictions and scheme-theoretic fibres

proof.text: If $\dim X_{i,s}\le d$, the open-subspace monotonicity lemma bounds every member of Step 1 by $d$. Conversely suppose all chart fibres have dimension at most $d$. For each $s$, the members with $s\notin V_{i,a}$ are empty and have dimension $-\infty\le d$; every other member has the chart bound. A scheme is sober by the generic-point lemma, hence quasi-sober and $T_0$, so the open-cover dimension lemma applies to $X_{i,s}$ and gives $\dim X_{i,s}\le d$. This proves (1), without any finite-type assumption.

Fix $a$ and $i\le j$, and put $P=W_{i,a}\times_{V_{i,a}}V_{j,a}$. Assume all fibres of $g_{i,a}$ have dimension at most $d$. For $t\in V_{j,a}$ write $s$ for its image in $V_{i,a}$. For every $y\in P_t$ with image $x\in(W_{i,a})_s$, the fibre base-change lemma, applied to the locally finite type morphism $g_{i,a}$, gives $\dim_y P_t=\dim_x(W_{i,a})_s$. Taking the whole old fibre as an open neighbourhood bounds the right side by $d$, by the definition of local dimension. Taking the supremum over $y$ gives $\dim P_t\le d$ by the global/local dimension lemma. If $P_t$ is empty the supremum is $-\infty$.

Let $c:W_{j,a}\hookrightarrow P$ be the assumed closed comparison, a morphism over $V_{j,a}$. Pull it back along $P_t\to P$. The closed-immersion base-change lemma gives a closed immersion $W_{j,a}\times_P P_t\hookrightarrow P_t$. The universal property identifies its source with $W_{j,a}\times_{V_{j,a}}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)=(W_{j,a})_t$: in either iterated pullback, maps from a scheme $T$ are exactly a map $u:T\to W_{j,a}$ and a map $v:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ whose composites to $V_{j,a}$ agree; the map to $P$ is forced to be $cu$. The two universal maps are inverse because their projections agree.

source.place: Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion, applied to the closed comparison

proof.text: A closed immersion identifies its source homeomorphically with a closed subspace. A strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of that subspace is also such a chain in the ambient space: closedness is transitive through the closed image and irreducibility uses the same induced topology. Consequently its dimension is at most the ambient dimension, including when the source is empty. Apply this to Step 4 and then Step 3 to obtain $\dim(W_{j,a})_t\le\dim P_t\le d$ for every $t$. This proves the persistence assertion in (2).

Choose $i_a$ for each $a$ in the finite set $A$. A common upper bound $j$ exists by induction on $A$: for the empty set choose any element of the nonempty $I$; to add $a$, use directedness on the previously obtained bound and $i_a$. For $k\ge j$, transitivity gives $k\ge i_a$ for every $a$, so the persistence just proved bounds every chart fibre of $g_{k,a}$ by $d$. Part (1) then bounds every fibre of $f_k$. If $A$ is empty, the covering assumption forces every $X_k$ empty; all fibre bounds hold, and the same arbitrary $j$ works.

Step 5 (closed subspace has smaller dimension) and step 6 (finite directed upper bound, including A=∅) are genuinely elementary.
